subject: Confusion in Actigraphy Data Analysis via GGIR - Discrepancy in Graphs

messages.author: cf781e2f132994ab
messages.subject: Confusion in Actigraphy Data Analysis via GGIR - Discrepancy in Graphs
parts:
Hello GGIR community,

I've recently gathered actigraphy data spanning a week, starting from Sunday afternoon and ending on the following Saturday afternoon. I've been using GGIR to analyze the data, but I'm encountering some confusion regarding the summary report.

My primary concern is with the first three graphs in the summary report. Despite the data collection period running from Sunday to Saturday, these graphs seem to display information only from Tuesday to Friday. This doesn't align with my expectations, as I should have data for all six nights.

Additionally, the last graph raises a specific issue. It appears to depict data up until Friday noon, while I would anticipate it to include data up to Saturday morning.

Any insights or guidance on why these discrepancies exist and how to rectify them would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Best regards,
Fatemeh Ghorbani

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Confusion in Actigraphy Data Analysis via GGIR - Discrepancy in Graphs
parts:
Hello Fatemeh,

On the one hand I would like to urge you to not expect too much from the visualreport.  We developed GGIR with a focus on the quantitative output as summarised in the csv report. The visualreport (pdf) is intended to give a quick impression of the data and is not necessarily an exact match of the quantitative analysis as conducted in the rest of GGIR.  There may be bugs in the visualisation that are not in the actual quantitative analysis.

On the other hand I am happy to try to identify the cause of your issue. Could you sent me:
  • Corresponding RData file in the meta/basic output folder
  • The part of your R script for running GGIR.

That said - If anybody wants to sponsor or apply for funding to enhance the visualisation functionalities in GGIR then please contact me.

Thanks,
Vincent

Hello,

Thank you for your thorough explanation. I've attached the file, and the code is provided below.

This is the script:

library(GGIR)
GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
  datadir="C:/Users/analysis/Data/P06/P06.bin",
  outputdir="C:/Users/analysis/Results/Results_P06_SD",
  # part 1 ----------
  f0=1,f1=2,
  studyname="TrainHorn",
  overwrite=TRUE,
  do.imp=TRUE,
  idloc=2,
  print.filename=FALSE,
  storefolderstructure=FALSE,
  #------------------------------
  #Part1 parameters:
  #------------------------------
  sensor.locationCharacter = "wrist",
  windowsizes=c(5,900,3600),
  use.temperature = TRUE,
  nonwear_approach = '2023',
  do.cal=TRUE,
  do.enmo=TRUE,
  do.anglez=TRUE,
  chunksize=1,
  printsummary=TRUE,
  #------------------------------
  #Part2 parameters:
  #------------------------------
  strategy=1,
  # ndayswindow=7,
  # hrs.del.start=1,
  # hrs.del.end=1,
  includedaycrit=24,
  L5M5window=c(0,24),
  M5L5res=10,
  winhr=c(5,10),
  qlevels=c(c(1020/1440),c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440),c(1435/1440)),
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  ilevels=c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
  mvpathreshold=c(100,120),
  #------------------------------
  #Part3 parameters:
  #------------------------------
  timethreshold=c(5,10),
  anglethreshold=5,
  ignorenonweaCr=TRUE,
  HASPT.algo = 'HDCZA',
  #------------------------------
  #Part4 parameters:
  #------------------------------
  excludefirstlast=FALSE,
  includenightcrit=20,
  sleeplog_used = TRUE,

  loglocation = "C:/Users/analysis/Sleep Diary/P06_SD.csv",
  relyonguider=FALSE,
  colid=1,
  coln1=4,
  do.visual=TRUE,
  #------------------------------
  #Part5 parameters:
  #------------------------------
  # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
  threshold.lig=c(30,40,50),
  threshold.mod=c(100,120),
  threshold.vig=c(400,500),
  boutcriter=0.8,
  boutcriter.in=0.9,
  boutcriter.lig=0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa=0.8,
  boutdur.in=c(10,20,30),
  boutdur.lig=c(1,5,10),
  boutdur.mvpa=c(1,5,10),
  timewindow=c("WW"),
  viewingwindow = 2,
  # ----------------------------------
  # Report generation
  # ------------------------------
  do.report=c(2,4,5))

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Confusion in Actigraphy Data Analysis via GGIR - Discrepancy in Graphs
parts:
Hi Fatemeh,

I just tried and if you specify only one instead of two sleep definitions the report should look better. Best approach may be to use the default values:
timethreshold=5,
anglethreshold=5,

It seems the visualreport is not capable of handling multiple sleep definitions yet. So, that could be a point for improvement. Please get in touch if you or anyone else wants to sponsor fixing this.

More generally speaking: When you see a problem always first try to check whether the problem also occurs with GGIR's default settings, which means running the GGIR call with a minimum number of input arguments and removing any old config.csv file in the output folder. 

Best,
Vincent
